Here's a description of lunchtime at little Punjab - plate after plate of mouth watering food being handed out with such love to customer after customer, everyone peacefully eating and talking in the area, and the place being sold out within a couple of hours of the lunch rush. Imagine how commendable that is when you have four things on the menu. The rajma and paneer chawal are marvellous. Ideal if you feel like having a home style meal in a mere 50 Bucks.

Little Punjab, a cute little open air joint tucked at the backside of SDA, it dishes out a short, sweet and simple menu at very reasonable price and provides sound quality stuff. It is quite a regular joint for my office colleagues and myself during lunch hours.
They serve home cooked rajma, chole, kadi, paneer along with chawal and the best part is all gravies are different in flavour with each one having its own signature.
The quantity size is apt and you can take a refill of the gravy if needed. All in all a very reasonable place for an on the go, stomach full lunch. Avoid it in hot weather as it can become very difficult the bear the sun.
If you want to quickly feed yourself with proper homely food without spending much and if you are in the locality, then Little Punjab is your best bet. It's quite good.
I just love the food. Its mouth watering. you can eat here each day of the week and still not get bored. The owner is very friendly . Recommeded for everyone who visits SDA

With every "North Indian" restaurant in Delhi peddling thick, greasy fare, this one is really special for NOT. If you turn up late, there are two very enterprising women who run a chai, maggi and bread pakoda shop just adjacent to Little Punjab. Skip chai, and choose customized maggi. Thank you.

Darjeeling momos (pork): delicious fluffy goodness, go so well with the spicy chutney served alongside - comfort food.

Momocha (chicken and pork): tiny momos swimming in a flavourful gravy. Amazing.

Shyapta (pork) and tingmo: this is a dish that goes really well with Speakeasy's whisky cocktails - the sliced pork is full of flavour and the tingmo is a great accompaniment.

Sel roti and...read more

Gurgoan has limited restaurants that serve Himalayan cuisine so I was thrilled to learn about Lungta, an extension of SpeakEasy. I always tell people that SpeakEasy has great food and the best Darjeeling momos apart from being a top notch bar for cocktails . We went to Lungta for lunch, we tried mutton and pork bhutun, Shyapta, Pork trotters, Momocha and Pork Thali . It took me back to Kathmandu and Darjeeling! Excellent food and another star for keeping it real and fresh. They have great staff, a clean comfy space and is really good value for money. This is going to be my fav hangout whenever I miss Nepali food. A must try this winter.

While walking towards subway to grab a light lunch, I see this new addition to speakeasy. Upon asking about it, its Nepali food! Without a second thought I walk in, eat a meal that 2 people could easily have between themselves and walk out much more happier than I would be going to subway. Had the pork based dishes. Great food!! Attaching a few photos. Yes 1 person ate all that. :D
Had food here & enjoyed it all, loved the pickles. Lungta cafe has a very warm feel to it. Congratulations to Yangdup & Minakshi for another new venture. Good luck.

A little background

Kunafa is a Levantine cheese pastry soaked in sweet sugar-based syrup . Usually eaten in Turkey for breakfast, though it is primarily considered a dessert.

Baklava is a rich, sweet pastry made of layers of filled with chopped nuts and sweetened and held together with syrup or honey.

Both the dishes are a must try recipe if you visit this restaurant.

Krispy Kreme is the only store in delhi that sells my beloved cake doughnuts! As much as I detest yeast doughnuts, I adore cake doughnuts and have been devouring Krispy Kreme from the time I lived in New York. Whats the difference? Yeast doughnuts are what people associate with doughnuts...they are the fluffy-airy light-brown doughnuts drizzled with icing on top. Moti Mahal Delux is one of the most oldest food chain present in delhi since 1947 not many people know Mr. Kundan Lal Guzral was the first who introduced butter chicken in this world.

Mr. Gujral realized that the Tandoori Chicken hanging on the seekhs above the tandoor all day would tend to dry out if unsold. He then came up with the genius idea of creating a basic gravy with tomatoes, butter, cream and some spices to immerse the Tandoori Chicken pieces in, helping them regain moisture and become palatable again and thus, was born The Butter Chicken.

My family and I bid adieu to 2015 with a memorable dinner at Mamagoto. The festive mood and feel of the place added to the delectable meal! For starters we ordered Chinese Sour and Pepper, Tom Yum Veg and Sweet Corn Soup....hands down the most delish soups ever! We also ordered Indonesian Grilled Chicken, Shrimps with Dry Red Chilli and Thai Crispy Vegetable - all fairly average in taste(Esp. Vegetarian). For main course we had the Hakka Noodles, Fried Rice (Bland and Ordinary), Garlic Chicken Curry and Veg Schezwan Curry. The Chicken curry was flavoursome and tasted wonderful but the vegetable curry again was average. Mamagoto is definitely one of the best Pan Asian restaurants in Delhi.
Overall awesome experience ! Highly recommend if you want to have healthy and tasty food. Excellent service and a menu with varieties of dishes to choose from!

This place never gets boring!! Since it established I have been to Mamagoto a numerous times and there is no flaw I have been able to point out when ever I dine there!!! Be it the food quality, the variety in food, the bar menu choice or the service.

Celebrating World Family Day with Thai & Japanese food was superb. My mother who herself is a decent cook and a beautiful home maker complimented the food and fell in love with the Cheese & asparagus sping rolls!

Never disappointed being here. Ambience, management, food and service is top notch!
High value for money for whatever you order.

Had a hearty lunch @ Mamagoto... The Fiery Thai Shrimp Fried rice with peppery Chicken ribbons and egg omelette bowled me over... I have been going to mamagoto for so long and am glad to say that nothing has changed. The food, the quality everything is the same.

I have eaten here before with normal-good experience with food and service; this particular event, though, needs special mention.

Would highly recommend this nice place!

This place has got to be in your must- visit - list.! And once you've been there, you will definitely want to go back again and again. Coz the food is that good!! Pros: Good food, nice Mocktails, pleasant staff.

A cozy colourful restaurant with a South Asian cuisine..

Random Sunday afternoon at Ambiance Mall. Lunch Time. Started walking around the food court.
At last I decided to try out at the Punjab cuisine. Ordered a Chicken Biriyani and a Lassi. It took a long time to get my order served.
The food was horrible. No masala or spices added in the Biriyani. Just rice mixed in some oil and two chicken pieces. Even the chicken peices were bad.
The Lassi was no where compared to the one I had in Amritsar. Actually it was the worst I have till date.
Never try this one. You have a lot of options out there in the food court.
